name: Electrical, plumbing and gas licensing and equipment safety
what: Hold a state licence for electrical, plumbing or gas work, issue compliance certificates, and register electrical equipment where required.
consistency_note: State licences, recognised in other states under automatic mutual recognition, except where a state has exempted an occupation.

basis.quote: building and trade work, such as a 'white card' for site access and licences for plumbing, gas fitting or electrical work
Registration as a responsible supplier under the Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS)

issues.what: What a plumbing or electrical licence lets you do differs by state, so a tradesperson working interstate under mutual recognition may still need a separate licence.

evidence.source: Building a skilled and adaptable workforce: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: Installation of fire protection equipment, such as sprinklers, is covered under a plumbing licence in Victoria but not in Western Australia. As a result, a plumber from Western Australia working in Victoria under AMR is not authorised to perform fire protection work without obtaining a separate licence in Victoria

evidence.source: Building a skilled and adaptable workforce: Inquiry report
evidence.quote: in some but not all jurisdictions, plumbers may undertake roofing and mechanical services or incidental electrical work

evidence.locator: Section C (Occupational licensing), key points, p. 89
evidence.quote: Not all states have joined the automatic mutual recognition scheme (Queensland does not participate), and states and territories continue to exclude some professions.

issues.status_note: Automatic mutual recognition began in 2021; Queensland does not take part.
